offer.say: Nell Haraldsen, I ref your beer league. Four nights a week I hang my coat on the floor of a room that smells of brooms, because there's one hook and Gord the linesman got there first. It's in the book. I've been writing it in the book.

options.text: Have you considered a smaller coat?
Hooks are low on my list right now.

book.say: You do now. Gus did. Gus read it every Monday and fixed one thing a month. Hook, chair, mirror, heater. In that order. He died. No, sorry. He moved to Florida. Same thing, for a ref room.

options.text: Then I'll start with the hook.

cheek.say: I've considered a smaller job. Then I remember how much I love calling icing on the Ice Holes.

decline.say: Understood. The floor's not going anywhere. Neither's my coat.

accepted.say: You're a gentleman and a scholar. Or a lady. I've only seen you on skates, I can't tell from the stands.

options.text: Got the hooks. Putting them up.

p_game.say: I'm going to hang my coat with great ceremony. I might hang it twice.

complete.say: Three officials, three coats, zero on the floor. I wrote it in the book. I underlined 'grateful'. I've never underlined anything in that book that wasn't a penalty.

options.text: Don't call icing on my team, then.

c_chair.say: Hook, chair, mirror, heater. Gus's order. You've done the hook. I'm not asking for the chair. I'm just saying it's next.

c_cheek.say: Oh, I'll call it twice now. Out of affection.

c_glad.say: You did. And I'll remember it the next time your D leaves the zone early.

done.say: Coat's on a hook. Life is good.
